“Last term, our class started a small garden behind the school hall. We turned the hard soil with small forks and pulled out the weeds. Mei See brought some bean seeds from home. We dug little holes, dropped in two seeds each, and covered them with earth. Every morning before class, we took turns to water the rows. At first, nothing came up, and we were worried. Then, after two weeks, tiny green shoots pushed through the soil. We measured them every Friday and wrote the heights in a notebook. By the end of term, the bean plants were taller than our knees. We picked the beans and cooked a simple soup in the canteen kitchen. Our head teacher said we could grow the garden again next year.”
What did Mei See bring from home?

(A) The film starts at eight o’clock.
(B) Children under seven go free.
(C) Tickets are cheaper before six.
(D) No outside drinks allowed.
Which notice explains a price rule for children?
questions.explanation: Children going free is a price rule for children.

questions.questionText:
Read the four short notices.
(A) Keep off the grass.
(B) Do not litter here.
(C) Please walk your dog on a lead.
(D) Take your rubbish home.
Which notice is about dogs?
questions.explanation: “Walk your dog on a lead” is about dogs.

questions.questionText:
Read the four short notices.
(A) The party will be in the hall.
(B) We will cut the cake at noon.
(C) Bring a plate and a spoon.
(D) Guests should arrive at eleven.
Which note tells you what to bring to a meal?
questions.explanation: A plate and a spoon are things to bring.

questions.questionText:
Read the four short notices.
(A) This door is for outgoing passengers.
(B) Please stand behind the yellow line.
(C) Tickets may be bought on the platform.
(D) Mind the gap between the train.
Which warning is about a dangerous gap?
questions.explanation: “Mind the gap” warns about the gap between train and platform.

questions.questionText:
Read the four short notices.
(A) Keep the pot near a window.
(B) Plant two seeds in each pot.
(C) Water the seeds once a day.
(D) Feed the plants after a month.
Which gardening instruction is about light?
questions.explanation: A window gives the plant light, so this instruction is about light.

questions.questionText:
Read the four short notices.
(A) The museum tour leaves at ten sharp.
(B) Leave large bags at the cloakroom.
(C) The cafe on the ground floor closes at three.
(D) Bring your student card for a discount.
Which notice would help a student save money?
questions.explanation: A student-card discount saves money.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“Every Saturday, Mr Chan opens his small workshop early. He cuts pieces of wood, smooths them and joins them together. By noon, a simple wooden box is ready. He gives many of his boxes away to neighbours.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?

options.label: A
options.text: A Man Who Makes Wooden Boxes.

questions.explanation: The paragraph is about a man who makes wooden boxes.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“The sea was calm. The small boat rocked gently. The old fisherman cast his net and waited. Slowly, he pulled it back. It was heavy. He smiled because it was full of silvery fish.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The fisherman pulls in a net full of fish, so the paragraph is about a good catch.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“Some people think bats are blind and scary. In fact, most bats come out only at night and eat insects. They use sound to find their way. Bats help farmers by eating harmful bugs.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The paragraph gives facts about bats.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“Last winter, the pond froze. The ducks could not find open water. The children brought corn and stood by the bank. The ducks swam up and ate from their hands.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The children feed the hungry ducks, so the paragraph is about helping them.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“First, spread a cloth on the table. Next, lay out the plates and cups. Then, put the food in the middle. Finally, ask everyone to sit down.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?

options.label: A
options.text: How to Set for a Meal.

questions.explanation: The steps describe laying the table for a meal.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“Long ago, people sent messages by pigeon. The birds flew fast and knew the way home. A small note was tied to their leg. Even today, some people keep homing pigeons as a hobby.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The whole paragraph is about carrying messages by pigeon.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“The little shop sells bread in the morning. At noon, it adds hot soup. In the evening, it closes early so the baker can rest.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The shop sells bread and soup, so it is a bakery.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“A spider built a web between two bushes. Every morning, it repaired the holes made by the wind. Flies soon stuck to the strong threads. The spider never left its post.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The paragraph is about a spider repairing its web.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“We climbed the hill before sunrise. At the top, we sat quietly. The sky turned pink, then gold, and the sun appeared over the sea. It was worth the early start.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The paragraph describes climbing to see the sun rise.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“Many town birds now nest on buildings instead of trees. They find small ledges and gaps. People sometimes put up wooden boxes to help them. These boxes give the birds a safe place to raise their chicks.”
What is the best title for this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The paragraph explains how people help city birds by providing nesting boxes.

questions.questionText: Your little sister wants to feed the animals at the park. Which sign should you look for?

options.label: B
options.text: Please do not feed the birds.

options.label: D
options.text: No ball games on the grass.

questions.explanation: A sign about feeding birds tells you whether feeding the animals is allowed.

questions.questionText: You want to borrow books on dinosaurs. Which place should you visit?
questions.explanation: A library lends books.

questions.questionText: It starts to rain heavily on your walk home. Which notice helps you find shelter?

options.label: A
options.text: Covered walkway to the mall — 50 m.

questions.explanation: A covered walkway gives shelter from the rain.

questions.questionText: You want to buy a birthday card. Which shop should you enter?

options.label: A
options.text: Paper Corner — cards, wraps and gifts.

questions.explanation: A shop selling cards and wraps sells birthday cards.

questions.questionText: Your class wants to get a small tree to plant at school. Which notice tells you where to get one?

options.label: A
options.text: Lost property on the first floor.

options.label: C
options.text: Free saplings at the garden office.

questions.explanation: Saplings are young trees.

questions.questionText: A visitor asks where to leave his large bag during a show. Which notice answers him?

options.label: A
options.text: Cloakroom — left luggage, second door on the left.

questions.explanation: A cloakroom is where bags are left.

questions.questionText: You want to know if the pool is open on a public holiday. Which notice helps?

options.label: A
options.text: Pool hours: closed on public holidays.

options.label: C
options.text: No diving in the shallow end.

questions.explanation: The notice about pool hours gives the opening times.

questions.questionText: A family wants a cheap meal and somewhere to park near the door. Which notice best suits them?

options.label: A
options.text: A la carte only, no reservations.

options.label: D
options.text: Family lunch set, free parking at the back.

questions.explanation: The family wants a cheap set meal and parking; this notice offers both.

questions.questionText:
Read the note.
“Hi Mei See, I will be late today. Please save me a seat near the window.”
Why did the writer write this note?

options.label: A
options.text: To ask a friend for a favour.

options.label: B
options.text: To invite someone to a party.

questions.explanation: The writer asks a friend to save a seat, which is a small favour.

questions.questionText:
Read the poster.
“Grand Sale! 50% off all toys this weekend only.”
The poster is mainly meant to
questions.explanation: A sale poster tries to persuade people to buy.

questions.questionText:
Read the note.
“We found a small tortoise near the pond. It has a yellow shell. If it is yours, call the school office.”
The writer wants to
questions.explanation: The note asks the owner to call, so the aim is to return the lost pet.

questions.questionText:
Read the leaflet.
“Drink water, rest your voice, and cover your mouth when you cough. A cold usually goes away in a few days.”
The leaflet mainly
questions.explanation: The leaflet gives tips for looking after yourself when you have a cold.

questions.questionText:
Read the card.
“Thank you for helping me carry my books that day. You are a true friend.”
The writer wrote this card to
questions.explanation: “Thank you” shows the writer is expressing thanks.

questions.questionText:
Read the advertisement.
“Learn the guitar in four weeks! Small classes, friendly teachers, first lesson free. Call 012-345 6789.”
The main purpose of the advertisement is to

options.label: B
options.text: persuade people to join a course.

options.label: C
options.text: tell a story about a guitar player.

questions.explanation: The advert invites people to sign up for guitar lessons.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“Many people throw away old bags. But an old bag can be cleaned and used again. It can carry lunch, books or toys. Why buy a new one when the old one is still strong?”
The writer wants readers to

options.label: B
options.text: reuse things instead of buying new.

questions.explanation: The writer argues that a strong old bag can be used again instead of being replaced.

questions.questionText:
Read the notice on a box.
“Fragile — handle with care. Keep this side up.”
The notice is meant to
questions.explanation: “Handle with care” warns people to be careful.

questions.questionText:
Read the message.
“The bus will leave at 8 a.m. sharp. Please arrive fifteen minutes earlier.”
The main purpose of this message is to

options.label: C
options.text: give clear arrangements for the trip.

questions.explanation: The message states the meeting time and instructions for the trip.

questions.questionText:
Read the paragraph.
“Some schools no longer use printed workbooks. Instead, students read on tablets. This saves paper and trees. However, children must remember to charge their devices every night.”
The writer’s main purpose is to

options.label: C
options.text: describe both sides of a change.

questions.explanation: The paragraph gives a benefit (saves paper) and a drawback (remembering to charge), so it balances both sides.

questions.questionText:
“Pass me the salt, please. And could you chop the onions?”
Where are the speakers most likely to be?
questions.explanation: Passing salt and chopping onions happen while cooking in a kitchen.

questions.questionText:
“The bell rang. The children stood up, pushed in their chairs and walked out talking loudly.”
What will the children probably do next?
questions.explanation: When the school bell rings and children leave chatting, they are going for a break.

questions.questionText:
“The man looked at his ticket, then at the big board. He frowned and checked his watch again. He asked the officer at the counter.”
The man is probably
questions.explanation: A ticket, a timetable board, a watch and a counter officer suggest a station and a worried traveller.

questions.questionText:
“She held the rope tightly, breathed in, and stepped to the edge. Her friends waved from below. For a moment she hesitated, then jumped.”
The writer is most likely
questions.explanation: A rope, friends below and a jump from an edge suggest a rope swing or ride.

questions.questionText:
“Every morning, the old shopkeeper swept the path outside his door. He knew the names of all his regular customers and always saved the warmest bread for them.”
We can say the shopkeeper was
questions.explanation: Remembering customers and saving the best bread for them shows he is kind and thoughtful.

questions.questionText:
“The rain had stopped, but the roads were still wet. Children jumped in the puddles and laughed. A rainbow hung low over the rooftops.”
The children felt
questions.explanation: Jumping in puddles and laughing shows they felt playful and cheerful.

questions.questionText:
“Your food will be ready in ten minutes. Please take a number and wait at the counter.”
The speaker is probably

options.label: A
options.text: an assistant in a food shop.

questions.explanation: Talking about food ready soon and taking a number sounds like a food shop.

questions.questionText:
“They packed tents, sleeping bags and tins of food. Father checked the map twice. Mother put extra torches in the bag. The children could not stop talking about the stars.”
The family was preparing to

options.label: D
options.text: visit a museum for a day.

questions.explanation: Tents, sleeping bags, a map, torches and talking about the stars all point to camping.

questions.questionText:
“He turned the page slowly. Sometimes he nodded, sometimes he smiled. At the end, he closed the book and sat in silence for a while.”
The man felt
questions.explanation: Nodding, smiling and sitting quietly at the end suggest he was moved by the book.

questions.questionText:
“The new girl sat alone at recess. She watched the others play but did not join in. When a boy waved, she looked away and opened her book.”
The girl was probably
questions.explanation: Sitting alone, watching and looking away suggest she was shy and unsure.

questions.questionText: “Zhi Hao pushed the garden gate, but it was rusty and would not move.” The word rusty means

options.label: C
options.text: affected by rust on old metal.

questions.explanation: A rusty gate is one covered in rust from age and damp.

questions.questionText: “Mei See felt gloomy on the rainy day because she could not go out to play.” The word gloomy means
questions.explanation: Being stuck inside on a rainy day makes a child feel gloomy, or sad and low.

questions.questionText: “The stream meandered through the field before it reached the old bridge.” The word meandered means
questions.explanation: A stream that meanders follows a slow, winding course.

questions.questionText: “The cook garnished the dish with a small sprig of parsley.” The word garnished means
questions.explanation: Garnishing means adding a small decoration such as a sprig of parsley.

questions.questionText: “Despite the dull weather, the hikers pressed on to the summit.” Here pressed on means
questions.explanation: “Pressed on” means kept going even when the weather was bad.

questions.questionText: “The kitten was timid and hid under the sofa when strangers came.” The word timid means
questions.explanation: A timid kitten hides because it is shy and easily frightened.

questions.questionText: “The teacher praised the class for their neat and careful work.” The word praised means
questions.explanation: To praise is to say someone has done well.

questions.questionText: “The speaker’s voice was barely audible over the noise of the crowd.” The word audible means
questions.explanation: Audible means able to be heard; “barely audible” means just loud enough to hear.

questions.questionText: “The old lorry coughed and spluttered before it finally started.” The word spluttered means
questions.explanation: An old engine splutters with small popping, choking sounds.

questions.questionText: “The signs at the crossing were ambiguous, so no one knew which gate to use.” The word ambiguous means

options.label: C
options.text: unclear, with more than one meaning.

questions.explanation: Ambiguous means unclear, allowing more than one reading.

questions.questionText:
Read the note.
"Hi Mei Yue, Please bring my water bottle tomorrow. It is on the kitchen table. Thank you! Siew Ching."
Why did Siew Ching write this note?

options.label: A
options.text: To invite Mei Yue to a birthday party.

options.label: B
options.text: To ask Mei Yue to bring her bottle.

options.label: C
options.text: To tell Mei Yue about a school trip.

options.label: D
options.text: To return a storybook to Mei Yue.

questions.explanation: Siew Ching needs Mei Yue to bring the water bottle that is on the kitchen table, so the note asks for this small favour.

questions.questionText:
Read the short text.
"Divya always shares her snacks with the new girl in class. She helps her carry books and smiles at everyone she meets."
What is Divya like?
questions.explanation: Sharing snacks and helping the new girl show that Divya is kind and friendly, not shy, rude or proud.

questions.questionText:
Read the notice.
"LOST — a small brown wallet with a cat sticker inside. If you find it, please call 012-345 6789. Thank you."
Why was this notice put up?

options.label: C
options.text: To invite friends to a party.

options.label: D
options.text: To ask people to help find a lost wallet.

questions.explanation: A lost notice asks the public to return or report a lost item; it is not for selling goods or inviting people.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Afiq stood at the front of the class. His hands shook. He looked at his shoes and could not remember his words."
How did Afiq feel?
questions.explanation: Shaking hands, looking at the shoes and forgetting the words are signs of nervousness, not excitement, pride or boredom.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Grandma Myna put some seeds in the soil in March. She watered them every day. In June, small green shoots came up and grew taller."
What most probably grew from the seeds?
questions.explanation: Seeds watered and tended in soil grow into plants; toys, books and stones do not grow from seeds.

questions.questionText:
Read the sign.
"PLEASE DO NOT FEED THE MONKEYS. They may become aggressive. Thank you."
What does this sign tell visitors?

options.label: A
options.text: To buy food for the monkeys.

options.label: D
options.text: To take photos of the monkeys.

questions.explanation: The sign asks visitors not to feed the monkeys, because feeding them may make the monkeys aggressive.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Chun Hoe arrived early for the concert. He helped carry the chairs and set up the stage. When everyone left, he stayed behind to pick up the rubbish."
What is Chun Hoe like?
questions.explanation: Arriving early, helping to set up and staying to clean up without being asked show Chun Hoe is helpful and responsible.

questions.questionText:
Read the email.
"Dear Irfan, Thank you very much for the book about dinosaurs. I read it twice already. It was the best birthday surprise ever. Love, Devan."
Why did Devan write this email?

options.label: A
options.text: To borrow more books from Irfan.

options.label: B
options.text: To invite Irfan to a party.

options.label: C
options.text: To thank Irfan for the birthday gift.

options.label: D
options.text: To ask Irfan for his homework.

questions.explanation: Devan thanks Irfan for the dinosaur book and calls it his best birthday surprise, so the email is a thank-you note.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Our night market opens at six in the evening. It is always crowded on Fridays. You can buy fresh fruit, cheap clothes and hot cooked food. It closes at ten at night."
Which statement is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The market opens in the evening.

options.label: B
options.text: The market is quiet on Fridays.

questions.explanation: The text says the market opens at six in the evening; the other choices contradict the text (crowded on Fridays, sells fruit/clothes/food, closes at ten).

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Meena saved her pocket money for many months. Every Saturday she stopped to look at the red bicycle in the shop window."
What will Meena most probably do?
questions.explanation: Saving money for months and looking at the same bicycle each week shows Meena wants to buy it, not sell, spend on sweets or move.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"The whole school cheered. Liau held up the silver cup high above his head. His teammates patted his back. He could not stop smiling."
How did Liau feel?
questions.explanation: Holding up the cup, being patted by teammates and smiling show pride and happiness, not sadness, fear or boredom.

questions.questionText:
Read the note.
"For my dear neighbour — these biscuits are from my kitchen. Please enjoy them! With love, Mrs Ong."
Why did Mrs Ong leave the basket?

options.label: A
options.text: To sell biscuits to the neighbour.

options.label: B
options.text: To share her homemade biscuits with the neighbour.

options.label: C
options.text: To ask the neighbour for money.

questions.explanation: The note gives the biscuits as a loving gift, so Mrs Ong is sharing them; she is not selling, asking for money or borrowing sugar.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Mr Tan closed his black umbrella, shook the water off it and looked at the wet street outside the window."
What was the weather like outside?

options.label: C
options.text: It was very hot and dry.

options.label: D
options.text: It was a clear, still night.

questions.explanation: A wet umbrella, shaking off water and a wet street all point to rain, not snow, heat or a clear night.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Kavya held the letter tightly. She read it again and again. Then she jumped up and ran to tell her grandmother the news."
The letter most probably brought her ___.
questions.explanation: Reading the letter twice, holding it tightly and running to share the news show Kavya was pleased, so the news was good, not a bill or a list.

questions.questionText:
Read the notice.
"SCHOOL CONCERT — Friday, 8 p.m. All parents are welcome. Tickets at the door, RM10 each."
What is the purpose of this notice?

options.label: B
options.text: To invite parents to come to the concert.

questions.explanation: The notice tells parents the time, price and venue of the concert and welcomes them, so its purpose is to invite them along.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Last weekend, Hani visited her uncle's farm. Every morning she walked to the duck pond and collected the warm eggs in a basket. Her uncle told her that the ducks lay more eggs when the weather is cool. Hani loved the quack of the ducks and the smell of the fresh eggs."
Which statement is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Hani bought the ducks in town.

options.label: B
options.text: The ducks lay more eggs when it is hot.

options.label: C
options.text: The ducks were kept on the farm.

options.label: D
options.text: Hani worked in a busy city office.

questions.explanation: The duck pond and collecting eggs on her uncle's farm show the ducks are kept there; her uncle says ducks lay more eggs in cool weather, so the 'hot' and 'city office' choices are wrong.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"On the first day, the new boy sat alone at the back during recess. Chee Keong noticed him, walked over and shared his food. The next day, he showed the new boy where the library and the canteen were."
What is Chee Keong most probably like?
questions.explanation: Sharing food with a lonely newcomer and showing him around the school are unstated clues that Chee Keong is kind and welcoming.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Anis walked to the counter with her library books. The librarian typed on the computer, frowned, wrote a number on a yellow slip and passed it across to Anis. Anis sighed and took out some coins from her purse."
What most probably happened?

options.label: C
options.text: Anis had to pay a small fine for late books.

options.label: D
options.text: Anis closed her library card forever.

questions.explanation: Typing the return date, a frown, a written slip and taking out coins all point to a small late-return fine; none of the other choices involves paying money.

questions.questionText:
Read the text.
"Mrs Chong's bakery opens at seven every morning. She mixes the flour at five, before anyone is awake. The smell of warm bread fills the street. On Saturdays, regular customers queue early for their favourite buns."
Which statement is true?

options.label: C
options.text: Mrs Chong starts work before the shop opens.

options.label: D
options.text: The bakery is closed on Saturdays.

questions.explanation: Mixing flour at five for a seven o'clock opening proves Mrs Chong starts before opening; the text says Saturdays are busy, so 'closed on Saturdays' is wrong.

questions.questionText:
Read the card.
"Dear Cikgu Rahman, We will never forget your funny stories and your patient help with our reading. Thank you for such a wonderful year. With love, Year 4 Mulia."
Why did the class write this card?

options.label: A
options.text: To invite him to a football match.

options.label: B
options.text: To thank their teacher at the end of the year.

options.label: C
options.text: To complain about too much homework.

options.label: D
options.text: To borrow a book from him.

questions.explanation: Thanking him for his stories, patient help and a 'wonderful year' shows this is an end-of-year thank-you card to the teacher, not an invitation or a complaint.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The cat slept _____ the warm cardboard box."
questions.explanation: Inside a box takes the preposition 'in'; we do not say on/at/by the box when the cat is inside it.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We go to the market _____ foot every Sunday."
questions.explanation: 'On foot' is the fixed phrase meaning walking; by foot is not used in BrE.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The old photograph hung _____ the wall above the sofa."
questions.explanation: Pictures are hung on the wall surface, so 'on' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The children waited _____ the big umbrella when the rain came."
questions.explanation: Shelter from rain is under an umbrella; over would mean above it, not sheltered by it.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"My cousin's birthday is _____ 12 April."
questions.explanation: Specific dates take 'on' (on 12 April); in is used for months/seasons, at for clock times.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We arrived _____ the bus station just as the bus left."
questions.explanation: Arrive at is used for small or specific places like a station; arrive in is for cities/countries.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The quiet village lies _____ two green hills."
questions.explanation: Between is used for two things (two hills); among is used for more than two, in a crowd.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"An old fisherman sat _____ the river, waiting quietly."
questions.explanation: 'By the river' means beside it; on/in the river would mean on or in the water itself.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"I have lived in Johor _____ 2019."
questions.explanation: Since + a point in time (2019); for is used with a length of time (for five years).

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We waited _____ nearly an hour for the late train."
questions.explanation: For + a length of time (an hour); since needs a starting point, not a duration.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"I wanted a cold drink, _____ there was no water left in the bottle."
questions.explanation: But shows a contrast (wanted a drink, yet none was left); so/because would give the wrong cause-effect.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"It rained heavily, _____ we stayed at home all afternoon."
questions.explanation: So shows the result of the rain (therefore we stayed in); because would reverse the cause.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Mei Yue _____ Siew Ching walk to school together every day."
questions.explanation: And joins two equal subjects (Mei Yue and Siew Ching); the other words do not join two names here.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We stayed indoors _____ it was raining outside."
questions.explanation: Because gives the reason for staying indoors; but/so/and do not express a reason.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Would you like a cup of tea _____ a glass of cold juice?"
questions.explanation: Or offers a choice between two drinks; the other conjunctions do not express a choice.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The test paper was quite hard, _____ Chun Hoe finished it first."
questions.explanation: But shows contrast (hard paper, yet he finished first); so would wrongly suggest the hardness caused speed.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The box was very heavy, _____ the two boys lifted it together."
questions.explanation: So shows the result: because it was heavy, they lifted it together.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"I did not go out to play _____ I had a slight headache."
questions.explanation: Because gives the reason for not going out; the other options give the wrong logic.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"She picked up her bag _____ ran quickly out of the door."
questions.explanation: And joins two actions in sequence (picked up and ran); the contrast/choice words do not fit.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We could not buy the toy car _____ we had spent all our pocket money."
questions.explanation: Because explains why they could not buy it; so would suggest not buying caused the spending, reversing the logic.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"That is my elder sister. _____ is twelve years old."
questions.explanation: Sister is female, so the subject pronoun 'She' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The boys are very hungry. _____ want their lunch now."
questions.explanation: The boys is plural, so the subject pronoun 'They' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"My kitten is small. _____ sleeps on my bed at night."
questions.explanation: An animal referred to neutrally takes 'It'; the plural/other pronouns do not match a single kitten.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"This is Devan's new school bag. It is _____."
questions.explanation: Devan is a boy, so the possessive 'his' agrees; her/their/its refer to other people or things.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Mei Yue could not find _____ pencil case this morning."
questions.explanation: Mei Yue is a girl, so the possessive 'her' agrees with the subject.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The children bought _____ mother a warm birthday card."
questions.explanation: The children is plural, so the possessive 'their' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"I met the two girls at the park and gave _____ some ripe mangoes."
questions.explanation: After a verb we need the object pronoun 'them'; they is a subject pronoun and their is possessive.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Keep this secret between you and _____."
questions.explanation: After 'between' we need the object pronoun 'me'; I is a subject pronoun and my/mine are possessive.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"My brother and _____ often cycle around the neighbourhood in the evening."
questions.explanation: As part of the subject we need 'I'; me is an object pronoun and my/mine are possessive.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The little bird fell from the branch, but _____ was not hurt at all."
questions.explanation: A single bird referred to neutrally takes the object/subject pronoun 'it'; he/she/they do not agree.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Every morning my father _____ to work by car."
questions.explanation: 'Every morning' shows a habit, so the present simple 'goes' (he/she/it) is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Look! The baby _____ peacefully in the cot right now."
questions.explanation: 'Look!' and 'right now' show an action happening now, so present continuous 'is sleeping' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Yesterday our class _____ to the science museum."
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' shows the past, so the past form 'went' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Last night, Mother _____ a delicious chocolate cake for tea."
questions.explanation: 'Last night' shows the past, so the regular past 'baked' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Listen! Someone _____ loudly on the front door."
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' shows an action happening now, so present continuous 'is knocking' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"I _____ my keys, so I had to wait outside the house."
questions.explanation: The waiting happened in the past, so the past 'lost' is correct; lose/loses are present forms.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"She was soaking wet because she _____ in the heavy rain without an umbrella."
questions.explanation: The whole scene is in the past, so the past 'stood' agrees with 'was'; stands/stand are present.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"When the lights suddenly went out, the children _____ afraid."
questions.explanation: 'The children' is plural and the event is past, so 'were' agrees; was/is/are are wrong for plural past.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The sun _____ in the east every day."
questions.explanation: A general truth uses the present simple; 'the sun' is singular, so 'rises' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We _____ an interesting documentary about sea turtles last Friday."
questions.explanation: 'Last Friday' shows the past, so the regular past 'watched' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"He _____ a deep breath and pushed open the heavy wooden door."
questions.explanation: The pushing is a past action, so the past 'took' is correct; takes/take/taking are present forms.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The pupils _____ down quietly and opened their new books."
questions.explanation: The opening of the books is a past action, so the past 'sat' agrees; sit/sits are present.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"There is too _____ sugar in this lemonade."
questions.explanation: 'Sugar' is uncountable, so 'too much' is correct; many/few are used with countable nouns.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"How _____ eggs do we need for the cake?"
questions.explanation: 'Eggs' are countable, so 'how many' is correct; much/little go with uncountable nouns.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"She bought two _____ of bread from the baker."
questions.explanation: 'Loaf' has the irregular plural 'loaves'; loafs/loafes are not correct BrE spellings.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The three _____ were playing noisily in the field."
questions.explanation: 'Child' has the irregular plural 'children'; childs/childrens are not real words.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"There are only a _____ eggs left, not enough to bake a cake."
questions.explanation: 'Eggs' are countable, so 'a few' is correct; little/much go with uncountable nouns.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Late at night, I saw three _____ running across the kitchen floor."
questions.explanation: 'Mouse' has the irregular plural 'mice'; mouses/mices are incorrect.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The _____ were peacefully grazing on the hill."
questions.explanation: 'Sheep' has the same form in the plural (one sheep, two sheep); sheeps/sheepes are wrong.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Can I have _____ orange juice, please?"
questions.explanation: In a polite request/offering we use 'some'; any is typical of questions/negatives, and many/a do not fit uncountable juice.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Yesterday I _____ my grandmother in her village."
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' shows the past, so the regular past 'visited' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Last Sunday we _____ to the bird park with our cousins."
questions.explanation: 'Last Sunday' shows the past, so the irregular past 'went' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"She _____ a beautiful song at the concert last night."
questions.explanation: 'Last night' shows the past, so the irregular past 'sang' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The children _____ loudly at the funny story."
questions.explanation: The story is already told, so the regular past 'laughed' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Mother _____ a warm dinner for us yesterday evening."
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday evening' shows the past, so the regular past 'cooked' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"I _____ my teeth and went to bed at nine."
questions.explanation: Going to bed is a past sequence, so the regular past 'brushed' agrees.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"They _____ games on the field after school yesterday."
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' shows the past, so the regular past 'played' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"My father _____ his car carefully last weekend."
questions.explanation: 'Last weekend' shows the past, so the regular past 'washed' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The bell _____ loudly and the pupils ran inside."
questions.explanation: Running inside is a past action, so the irregular past 'rang' agrees.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"I _____ my project before dinner yesterday."
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' shows the past, so the regular past 'finished' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"She _____ a lovely picture of her cat in art class."
questions.explanation: The art lesson is over, so the irregular past 'drew' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We _____ the train to the city last week."
questions.explanation: 'Last week' shows the past, so the irregular past 'took' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Suddenly, the children _____ a strange noise outside."
questions.explanation: The event is over, so the irregular past 'heard' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"He _____ off his bicycle and hurt his knee."
questions.explanation: The accident is a past event, so the irregular past 'fell' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Grandma _____ very tired after the long walk home."
questions.explanation: The walk is over, so the irregular past 'felt' agrees with the past state.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We _____ a tiny kitten behind the old workshop."
questions.explanation: The discovery is in the past, so the irregular past 'found' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Our teacher _____ us a story about a brave sailor."
questions.explanation: The story was told in the past, so the irregular past 'told' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"He _____ his way in the busy night market."
questions.explanation: Getting lost is a past event, so the irregular past 'lost' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We _____ our suitcases and left for the station."
questions.explanation: Leaving for the station is a past sequence, so the regular past 'packed' agrees.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The little shop _____ at nine and closed at six."
questions.explanation: The opening and closing happened in the past, so 'opened' agrees.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"I _____ my best friend a present for her birthday."
questions.explanation: The birthday is over, so the irregular past 'gave' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"It was raining, so she _____ her umbrella to school."
questions.explanation: Bringing the umbrella happened in the past, so 'brought' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"We _____ breakfast at seven this morning."
questions.explanation: 'This morning' (now past) takes the irregular past 'had'.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"She _____ goodbye to us and walked to the gate."
questions.explanation: Walking to the gate is a past action, so the regular past 'waved' agrees.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The dog _____ the slipper all the way back home."
questions.explanation: Bringing back the slipper is a past action, so 'fetched' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"I _____ a long letter to my cousin last month."
questions.explanation: 'Last month' shows the past, so the irregular past 'wrote' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"The nurse _____ the tiny baby gently in her arms."
questions.explanation: The past of hold is the irregular 'held', not 'holded'; hold/holding are not past forms.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"When twelve o'clock came, the old clock _____ twelve times."
questions.explanation: The past of strike is the irregular 'struck', not 'striked'.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Our team _____ the football match last Saturday."
questions.explanation: The past of win is the irregular 'won'; 'winned' is not a real word.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct word.
"Yesterday I _____ the red apple, not the green one."
questions.explanation: The past of choose is the irregular 'chose'; choosed is wrong and chosen is a participle, not the past.

questions.questionText: Mei Ying sees an elderly woman carrying a heavy basket at the market. What should Mei Ying say to offer help?

options.label: B
options.text: Would you like some help with your basket?

options.label: C
options.text: Why is your basket so heavy?

options.label: D
options.text: I cannot carry it for you.

questions.explanation: An offer is a polite way of asking if someone would like help, not an order or a question.

questions.questionText: Devi notices her friend Siew Lan shivering in the cold classroom. Devi has an extra jacket in her bag. What is the best offer?

options.label: C
options.text: You can borrow my jacket if you like.

questions.explanation: Offering something you have (an extra jacket) in a polite way is a real offer.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is an invitation to a birthday party?

options.label: B
options.text: I have bought a big cake.

options.label: D
options.text: Please come to my birthday party on Saturday.

questions.explanation: An invitation asks someone to come; the other sentences only state facts.

questions.questionText: Kamal wants to invite his classmate David to watch a cartoon after school. Which sentence sounds like a real invitation?

options.label: A
options.text: Shall we watch a cartoon together after school?

options.label: D
options.text: The cinema is far from here.

questions.explanation: 'Shall we...?' is a common way to invite someone to do something together.

questions.questionText: Rina sees her neighbour Fong struggling to carry a bicycle up the stairs. What should Rina say?

options.label: B
options.text: Do you ride your bike often?

options.label: C
options.text: Would you like me to help you carry it?

questions.explanation: Offering help with 'Would you like me to...?' is polite and direct.

questions.questionText: Anna wants to invite Arul to her house on Sunday to bake cookies. Which sentence is the invitation?

options.label: B
options.text: Please come to my house on Sunday and we can bake cookies together.

questions.explanation: The invitation tells the person when to come and what they will do together.

questions.questionText: Chuen drops his pile of books on the floor. Lisa wants to help him. What should she say?

options.label: A
options.text: Your books are on the floor.

options.label: B
options.text: Why did you drop your books?

options.label: C
options.text: I am reading a book too.

options.label: D
options.text: Let me help you pick up your books.

questions.explanation: 'Let me help...?' offers help directly and politely.

questions.questionText: Nisha says, "Would you like to join us for a picnic at the park tomorrow?" Which reply accepts the invitation politely?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, I'd love to. What time shall we meet?

options.label: B
options.text: No, I do not like picnics.

questions.explanation: Accepting politely means saying yes warmly and showing interest.

questions.questionText: Tan offers Lily his seat on the crowded bus. Lily's arms are full of shopping bags. What should Lily say to accept?

options.label: C
options.text: Thank you, that is very kind of you.

options.label: D
options.text: Why are you giving me your seat?

questions.explanation: A polite acceptance thanks the person and shows appreciation.

questions.questionText: Mei invites Suresh to the fun fair, but Suresh feels unwell and cannot go. Which reply declines the invitation politely?

options.label: A
options.text: No way, I hate fun fairs.

options.label: B
options.text: I would love to come, but I am not feeling well. Maybe another time?

options.label: C
options.text: I am not going, ask someone else.

questions.explanation: A polite decline says sorry, gives a reason, and leaves the door open for another time.

questions.questionText: It starts to rain heavily. Arul has two umbrellas in his bag. What is the best offer to his classmate?

options.label: D
options.text: You can share my umbrella if you like.

questions.explanation: Offering to share something useful is a natural, kind offer.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is an offer, not just a plain statement?

options.label: A
options.text: I have two tickets for the concert.

options.label: C
options.text: Can I get you a drink before the show?

options.label: D
options.text: We are going to the concert.

questions.explanation: 'Can I get you...?' is an offer; the others only give information.

questions.questionText: Chee Keong wants to invite his cousin to his house-warming open house. Which sentence is the invitation?

options.label: A
options.text: My new house is on Jalan Merdeka.

options.label: B
options.text: Please come to my open house this Sunday and see my new home.

options.label: C
options.text: I moved to a new house last month.

options.label: D
options.text: The house has a small garden.

questions.explanation: An invitation states the event and asks the person to attend.

questions.questionText: Chuen helps Nisha carry her large art folder to the art room. Nisha wants to thank him. What should she say?

options.label: A
options.text: Thank you for helping me with my folder.

questions.explanation: After someone offers help, a polite thank-you is the natural response.

questions.questionText: David invites Rina to join the school swimming club, but Rina has piano lessons on club days. Which reply declines politely?

options.label: D
options.text: Thank you for asking, but I have piano lessons on club days. Perhaps next term?

questions.explanation: A polite decline thanks the inviter, gives a real reason, and suggests another time.

questions.questionText: At the school canteen, Siew Lan has finished her lunch while Kamal is still in the queue. She notices he has not bought any water. Which is the most natural offer?

options.label: B
options.text: You should bring water next time.

options.label: C
options.text: Would you like a bottle of water? I have an extra one in my bag.

questions.explanation: The best offer notices the need and provides something helpful without sounding like a scold.

questions.questionText: Anna's grandfather is trying to read the small print on a medicine bottle but he cannot see the words clearly. Anna is holding a reading lamp nearby. Which offer is most suitable?

options.label: B
options.text: Grandpa, would you like me to read the label for you?

questions.explanation: The offer matches the real need (reading small print) and is respectful.

questions.questionText: A new student, Devi, sits alone at recess. Arul wants to invite her to sit with his group. Which sentence is the warmest invitation?

options.label: A
options.text: We have an extra seat. Would you like to join us for recess?

questions.explanation: A warm invitation points out an open space and directly asks the person to join.

questions.questionText: Read the paragraph. "First, we mix the flour and eggs in a bowl. ____, we pour the mixture into a baking tin. Finally, we put the tin in the oven." Which word fits the blank?
questions.explanation: In a step-by-step paragraph, 'First... Then... Finally' shows the order.

questions.questionText: Read: "Mei Ying has a cat. ____ is white and fluffy." Which pronoun fits the blank?
questions.explanation: 'It' refers back to the cat (a singular animal).

questions.questionText: Read: "We wanted to play outside, ____ it started to rain." Which joining word fits the blank?
questions.explanation: 'But' shows a contrast: they wanted to play outside, yet it rained.

questions.questionText: Read: "The students became quiet ____ the teacher walked in." Which word fits the blank?
questions.explanation: 'When' shows the time the two actions happen together.

questions.questionText: Read: "Devi bought a new notebook. ____ put it in her school bag." Which pronoun fits the blank?
questions.explanation: 'She' refers back to Devi, a girl.

questions.questionText: Read: "I stayed at home ____ I had a fever." Which joining word fits the blank?
questions.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for staying at home.

questions.questionText: Read: "Kamal lost his water bottle. ____ he looked for it everywhere." Which word fits the blank?
questions.explanation: 'After that' continues the story in order.

questions.questionText: Read: "There are three apples on the plate. ____ are for the visitors." Which pronoun fits the blank?
questions.explanation: 'They' refers back to the three apples (plural, as the subject).

questions.questionText: Read: "The film was very funny, ____ everyone laughed." Which joining word fits the blank?
questions.explanation: 'So' shows the result: the film was funny, and as a result everyone laughed.

questions.questionText: Read: "Last Sunday, Fong went to the bird park. ____, he watched the colourful parrots. Next, he had a cool drink. ____, he took the bus home." Which pair of words fits the blanks?
questions.explanation: 'First... Next... Finally' tells the order of the day.

questions.questionText: Read: "Mei Ying baked a cake. ____ was chocolate. She gave a slice to Devi. ____ was very happy." Which pair fits the blanks?
questions.explanation: 'It' refers to the cake; 'She' refers to Devi.

questions.questionText: Read: "The old man could not lift the heavy box. ____, two schoolboys stopped to help ____." Which pair fits the blanks?
questions.explanation: 'So' shows the result; 'him' refers to the old man as the object.

questions.questionText: Read: "Rina wanted to buy a storybook, ____ she did not have enough money. ____ she borrowed one from the library." Which pair fits the blanks?
questions.explanation: 'But' shows the contrast; 'So' shows the result of borrowing instead.

questions.questionText: Read: "The farmers grew fresh vegetables. ____ sold ____ at the market every Saturday." Which pair fits the blanks?
questions.explanation: 'They' is the subject (farmers); 'them' is the object (vegetables).

questions.questionText: Read: "David forgot his lunchbox at home. ____ he shared his friend's noodles ____." Which pair fits the blanks?
questions.explanation: 'So' shows the result; 'instead' shows he did one thing in place of another.

questions.questionText: Read: "Anna practised the piano every day. ____, she played beautifully in the concert." Which phrase fits the blank?
questions.explanation: 'As a result' links the practice to the good performance.

questions.questionText: Read: "Arul saw a little girl crying by the gate. ____ had lost ____ mother." Which pair fits the blanks?
questions.explanation: 'She' refers to the little girl; 'her' shows the mother belongs to her.

questions.questionText: Read: "We planted a small tree behind the house. ____ we watered ____ every morning." Which pair fits the blanks?
questions.explanation: 'After that' continues the order; 'it' refers to the tree.

questions.questionText: Read: "Nisha did not study for the test. ____ she did not do well in it." Which word fits the first blank?
questions.explanation: 'So' shows the result of not studying.

questions.questionText: Read: "Tan woke up early. He brushed his teeth and washed his face. ____, he walked to the bus stop. The bus arrived late, ____ he reached school just before the bell." Which pair fits best?
questions.explanation: 'Then' continues the order of the morning; 'so' shows the result of the late bus.

questions.questionText: Read: "The library was closed, ____ Mei Ying could not borrow the books. She walked home ____ she felt a little sad." Which pair fits?
questions.explanation: 'So' shows the result; 'and' joins the two actions of walking home and feeling sad.

questions.questionText: Read: "Devi carried a tray of drinks. ____ slipped and nearly dropped ____, ____ David caught the tray just in time." Which pair fits the first and third blank?
questions.explanation: 'She' refers to Devi; 'but' shows the contrast between slipping and David catching the tray.

questions.questionText: Which list of foods uses commas correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: I bought apples oranges and bananas.

options.label: B
options.text: I bought apples oranges, and bananas.

options.label: C
options.text: I bought apples, oranges, and bananas.

options.label: D
options.text: I bought, apples oranges and bananas.

questions.explanation: Items in a list are separated by commas: apples, oranges, and bananas.

questions.questionText: Which of these endings is correct?
questions.explanation: A question ends with a question mark.

questions.questionText: Which of these sentences begins with a capital letter?

options.label: A
options.text: my brother goes to bed at nine.

options.label: B
options.text: My brother goes to bed at nine.

options.label: C
options.text: My Brother goes to bed at nine.

options.label: D
options.text: my Brother goes to bed at nine.

questions.explanation: The first word of a sentence starts with a capital letter; common nouns like 'brother' do not.

questions.questionText: Which list uses commas correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: On the table there is a pen a ruler, and two books.

options.label: B
options.text: On the table, there is a pen a ruler and two books.

options.label: C
options.text: On the table there is, a pen, a ruler, and two books.

options.label: D
options.text: On the table there is a pen, a ruler and two books.

questions.explanation: Each item in the list is separated by a comma.

questions.questionText: Which of these sentences needs a full stop at the end?
questions.explanation: A statement like 'I live in Kuala Lumpur' ends with a full stop; questions end with a question mark.

questions.questionText: Which sentence shows commas in a list properly?

options.label: A
options.text: The box contains a torch a rope and a bottle of water.

options.label: B
options.text: The box, contains a torch, a rope and a bottle of water.

options.label: C
options.text: The box contains a torch, a rope, and a bottle of water.

options.label: D
options.text: The box contains a, torch, a rope, and a bottle of water.

questions.explanation: List items (torch, rope, bottle of water) are separated by commas.
questions.subtopic: Punctuation: commas in lists and end marks

questions.questionText: Which sentence ends with an exclamation mark correctly?
questions.explanation: An exclamation ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has correct punctuation?

options.label: A
options.text: On Sunday, we ate rice fish and vegetables for lunch.

options.label: B
options.text: On Sunday we ate, rice, fish, and vegetables, for lunch.

options.label: C
options.text: On Sunday we ate rice, fish, and, vegetables for lunch.

options.label: D
options.text: On Sunday we ate rice, fish, and vegetables for lunch.

questions.explanation: The list of foods has commas; there are no extra commas.
questions.subtopic: Punctuation: commas in lists and end marks

questions.questionText: Which sentence capitalises names of places and days properly?

options.label: A
options.text: We visited Penang Hill last Saturday.

options.label: B
options.text: We visited penang hill last saturday.

options.label: C
options.text: We visited Penang hill last saturday.

options.label: D
options.text: we visited Penang Hill last Saturday.

questions.explanation: Names of places and days, and the first word of a sentence, need capital letters.
questions.subtopic: Punctuation: commas in lists and end marks

questions.questionText: Which of these sentences has the correct commas in its list?

options.label: A
options.text: Mei bought a pen a pencil and an eraser from the shop.

options.label: B
options.text: Mei bought, a pen, a pencil and an eraser, from the shop.

options.label: C
options.text: Mei bought a pen, a pencil, and an eraser from the shop.

options.label: D
options.text: Mei bought a, pen, a pencil, and an eraser from the shop.

questions.explanation: Each item in the list is separated by a comma; no extra commas around the verb.
questions.subtopic: Punctuation: commas in lists and end marks

questions.questionText: Which of these sentences needs a question mark?

options.label: A
options.text: The shop opens at nine o'clock.

options.label: C
options.text: I am going to the market.

questions.explanation: 'When does the shop open' is a question, so it needs a question mark.
questions.subtopic: Punctuation: commas in lists and end marks

questions.questionText: Which list is punctuated correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: In the cupboard, we found cups plates bowls and glasses.

options.label: B
options.text: In the cupboard we found, cups, plates, bowls, and glasses.

options.label: C
options.text: In the cupboard we found cups plates, bowls and, glasses.

options.label: D
options.text: In the cupboard we found cups, plates, bowls, and glasses.

questions.explanation: Each item in the list (cups, plates, bowls, glasses) has a comma.
questions.subtopic: Punctuation: commas in lists and end marks

questions.questionText: Which sentence has a mistake in punctuation?

options.label: A
options.text: Do you like mangoes, papayas, or durians

options.label: B
options.text: My father reads the newspaper every morning.

options.label: C
options.text: The cat sat on the mat.

questions.explanation: This is a question, so it needs a question mark at the end.
questions.subtopic: Punctuation: commas in lists and end marks

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?

options.label: A
options.text: For breakfast, I had toast eggs and a glass of milk.

options.label: B
options.text: For breakfast I had, toast, eggs, and a glass, of milk.

options.label: C
options.text: For breakfast I had toast, eggs, and a glass of milk.

options.label: D
options.text: For breakfast I had toast eggs, and a glass of milk.

questions.explanation: List items (toast, eggs, a glass of milk) are separated by commas.
questions.subtopic: Punctuation: commas in lists and end marks

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the right capitals and ends with a full stop?

options.label: A
options.text: mr tan lives in jalan roch.

options.label: B
options.text: Mr Tan lives in Jalan Roch.

options.label: C
options.text: Mr tan lives in jalan Roch.

options.label: A
options.text: It keeps us fit and it does not pollute the air.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a slow way to travel.

questions.explanation: A good reason explains why the opinion is true and supports it.

options.label: B
options.text: In my opinion, Saturday is the best day of the week.

options.text: The sun rises in the east.

questions.explanation: 'In my opinion' signals a personal view, not a plain fact.

questions.questionText: Which reason supports the opinion "We should keep our classroom clean"?

options.text: We study in the classroom every day.

options.label: C
options.text: A clean classroom makes us feel good and helps us study.

questions.questionText: Which is a plain FACT, not an opinion?

questions.questionText: Which sentence gives a clear opinion with a reason?

options.label: D
options.text: Trees give us shade and fresh air.

questions.explanation: A good reason explains the benefit of planting trees.

questions.questionText: Your friend says, "I think our school uniform should be colourful." Which reply gives a different opinion with a reason politely?

options.text: I disagree. Plain uniforms look neat and they are easy to wash.

options.text: The market is near my house.

questions.questionText: Which reason best supports the opinion "Everyone should drink enough water every day"?

options.text: We eat three meals a day.

questions.explanation: A strong reason explains the wider problem behind the opinion.

questions.explanation: 'In my view' gives the opinion; 'because' gives two linked reasons.

questions.questionText: The kitchen was spotless. Every plate was clean and there was no dirt anywhere. What does 'spotless' mean?
questions.explanation: The next sentence says every plate is clean and there is no dirt, so spotless means very clean.

questions.questionText: The farmer planted the seeds in neat rows. Soon small green shoots came up from the soil. What does 'shoots' mean here?
questions.explanation: Seeds grow up into small green shoots, which are young new plants.

questions.questionText: My grandma told us a tale about a clever monkey. We listened quietly for ten minutes. What does 'tale' mean?
questions.explanation: Grandma tells children a tale, and they listen to it, so a tale is a story.

questions.questionText: The bus was crowded. People stood close together and there were no empty seats. What does 'crowded' mean?
questions.explanation: No empty seats and people standing close together show the bus is full of people.

questions.questionText: The food was delicious. Everyone at the table asked for more. What does 'delicious' mean?
questions.explanation: People ask for more when the food tastes very good.

questions.questionText: Please whisper in the library. Other children are reading and we must be quiet. What does 'whisper' mean?
questions.explanation: In a library we must be quiet, so whisper means to speak very softly.

questions.questionText: The river is shallow near the bank. Children can stand in it without swimming. What does 'shallow' mean?
questions.explanation: Children can stand in it, so the water is not deep.

questions.questionText: The box was heavy. The boy needed both hands to carry it. What does 'heavy' mean?
questions.explanation: He needs both hands to carry it, so the box weighs a lot.

questions.questionText: It began to pour. Soon the ground was all wet and the children ran inside. What does 'pour' mean here?
questions.explanation: The ground became all wet quickly, so it rained very hard.

questions.questionText: The film was boring. We almost fell asleep while watching it. What does 'boring' mean?
questions.explanation: People almost fall asleep when something is not interesting.

questions.questionText: She found a tiny kitten behind the bush. It was smaller than her hand. What does 'tiny' mean?
questions.explanation: It was smaller than her hand, so tiny means very small.

questions.questionText: The old wooden bridge wobbled when we walked on it. We held the rope tightly. What does 'wobbled' mean?
questions.explanation: We held the rope tightly because the bridge moved unsteadily from side to side.

questions.questionText: The pupils lined up in an orderly queue. No one pushed and everyone waited their turn. What does 'orderly' mean?
questions.explanation: No one pushed and everyone waited, so the queue was neat and well-behaved.

questions.questionText: Her grandmother passed away last year. The family still talks about her kind smile. What does 'passed away' mean?
questions.explanation: The family still talks about her in the past, so 'passed away' means died.

questions.questionText: The thieves stole the painting and left the museum during the night. What does 'thieves' mean?
questions.explanation: They stole the painting, so thieves are people who steal things.

questions.questionText: The lake was calm. Not a single wave moved on the water all morning. What does 'calm' mean here?
questions.explanation: No waves moved, so the water was still and quiet.

questions.questionText: We had to abandon the picnic because the rain came suddenly and was very heavy. What does 'abandon' mean?
questions.explanation: Because of the heavy rain, they gave up the picnic.

questions.questionText: The teacher praised the boy for his neat homework. He smiled and went back to his seat happily. What does 'praised' mean?
questions.explanation: He smiled happily, so the teacher said good things about his work.

questions.questionText: The soup was too salty. Mother added more water to make it taste better. What does 'salty' mean here?
questions.explanation: Mother added water to balance the taste, so it had too much salt.

questions.questionText: The rocket soared into the sky and became a tiny dot far above us. What does 'soared' mean?
questions.explanation: It became a tiny dot far above, so it flew high and fast.

questions.questionText: My little brother is very naughty. He draws on the walls and hides my pens. What does 'naughty' mean?
questions.explanation: Drawing on walls and hiding pens are bad behaviour, so naughty means behaving badly.

questions.questionText: The speaker's voice was faint. People sitting at the back could hardly hear her at all. What does 'faint' mean?
questions.explanation: People at the back could hardly hear her, so the voice was quiet and weak.

questions.questionText: The company donated books to the small village school. The children clapped their hands happily. What does 'donated' mean?
questions.explanation: The children were happy to receive the books, so the company gave them as a gift.

questions.questionText: He hesitated before answering the question because he was not quite sure of the answer. What does 'hesitated' mean?

questions.questionText:
Read the little poem.  
'The sun is up, the birds all sing,  
Let's run and play till evening!'  
How does the poem make you feel?
questions.explanation: Running and playing in the sunshine with singing birds makes the reader feel happy.

questions.questionText: The girl held her broken toy and tears ran down her face. How did she feel?
questions.explanation: Tears running down her face show she is sad about her broken toy.

questions.questionText: When the boy won the race, he threw his arms up in the air and grinned widely. How did he feel?
questions.explanation: Throwing his arms up and grinning show that he is proud of winning.

questions.questionText: The little dog heard the loud thunder and quickly ran under the bed. How did the dog feel?
questions.explanation: Running under the bed shows the dog is scared of the thunder.

questions.questionText:
Read the little rhyme.  
'Rain, rain, go away,  
Come again another day.'  
How does the child in the rhyme feel about the rain?
questions.explanation: The child asks the rain to 'go away', so the child wants it to stop.

questions.questionText: On the first day of school, her hands felt cold and her tummy did not feel right. How did she feel?
questions.explanation: Cold hands and a funny tummy on the first day show she is nervous.

questions.questionText: The children saw the big roller coaster rush past and shouted 'Again! Again!' How did they feel?
questions.explanation: Shouting 'Again!' shows they loved the ride and felt excited.

questions.questionText: The night was very dark. Something moved in the bushes nearby. The boy walked slowly all the way home. How did he feel?
questions.explanation: The dark night and moving bushes make the boy walk slowly, so he feels afraid.

questions.questionText: She spent a whole hour on her drawing. When she showed it to her mother, her mother said, 'What lovely colours!' How did she feel?
questions.explanation: Her mother praised the drawing, so she felt pleased.

questions.questionText:
Read the little poem.  
'My cat sits on the window seat,  
She purrs and purrs and purrs.'  
How does this poem make you feel?
questions.explanation: A purring cat on a warm window seat gives a calm and cosy feeling.

questions.questionText: It was the day of the concert. His knees shook a little and his mouth felt dry. How did he feel?
questions.explanation: Shaking knees and a dry mouth before performing show he is nervous.

questions.questionText: The old oak tree fell down in the storm. The children sat quietly and looked at the stump. How did they feel?
questions.explanation: They sat quietly at the stump of their old tree, so they felt disappointed.

questions.questionText: When the results were read out, she jumped up and down and hugged her best friend. How did she feel?
questions.explanation: Jumping up and down and hugging her friend show she is delighted.

questions.questionText: The little puppy wagged its tail quickly and licked the girl's hand. How would you feel if this happened to you?
questions.explanation: A friendly puppy wagging its tail and licking your hand makes you feel happy.

questions.questionText: He forgot his words on the stage. His face went red and he wanted to hide behind the curtain. How did he feel?
questions.explanation: A red face and wanting to hide show he is embarrassed.

questions.questionText:
Read the little poem.  
'Wind in the trees, leaves spinning round,  
Autumn is here, the best time around.'  
How does the poet feel about autumn?
questions.explanation: The poet calls autumn 'the best time around', so the poet enjoys it.

questions.questionText: They waited for the bus for a whole hour. The bus was full and did not even stop. How did they feel?
questions.explanation: Waiting an hour and being ignored by a full bus makes them feel frustrated.

questions.questionText: The present was wrapped in shiny paper. The boy shook it carefully. He did not open it yet, but his smile grew wider and wider. Why did his smile grow wider?

options.label: D
options.text: he was excited and curious about the gift

questions.explanation: Shaking the present and smiling show he is excited and curious before opening it.

questions.questionText: After the storm, the children found a small bird with a broken wing. They fed it and kept it warm. When the bird flew away a week later, the children were quiet for a while. How did they feel when it flew away?

options.label: A
options.text: a little sad but happy it was well

questions.explanation: They were quiet because they would miss the bird, but they were also glad it was well enough to fly.

questions.questionText:
Read the little poem.  
'Do not break the spider's web,  
Do not step upon the ant;  
Every small thing has its home,  
Just as you have yours.'  
What feeling does the poem want you to have?
questions.explanation: The poem asks you not to harm small creatures because they have homes too.

questions.questionText: The guide words at the top of a dictionary page are 'cat' and 'dog'. Which word would be found on this page?
questions.explanation: A page runs from 'cat' to 'dog'; 'cow' comes after cat and before dog in alphabetical order.

questions.questionText: In a dictionary, words are in alphabetical order. Which word comes FIRST?
questions.explanation: map < milk < moon < nose, so 'map' comes first.

questions.questionText:
Look at this dictionary entry:  
run /rʌn/ verb: to move quickly on foot.  
What does the word 'verb' tell you?

options.label: A
options.text: what type of word it is

questions.explanation: 'Verb' tells you the type of word it is - an action word.

questions.questionText: Which word comes immediately after 'orange' in a dictionary?
questions.explanation: apple, onion and owl all start with letters before p; pear starts with p, so it comes after orange.

questions.questionText: The guide words on a dictionary page are 'book' and 'box'. Which word is NOT on this page?
questions.explanation: The page runs from book to box; 'bus' comes after box, so it is on the next page.

questions.questionText:
Look at this dictionary entry:  
happy /ˈhæpi/ adjective: feeling pleasure.  
What does /ˈhæpi/ show?
questions.explanation: The letters between slashes show the pronunciation - how to say the word.

questions.questionText: In a dictionary, an entry says 'unhappy see happy'. Where should you look to understand 'unhappy'?
questions.explanation: The entry tells you to see 'happy', so the full meaning is under 'happy'.

questions.questionText: The guide words on a dictionary page are 'play' and 'pull'. Which word belongs on this page?
questions.explanation: paper and pink come before play, and queue comes after pull; pond (p-o) sits between play (p-l) and pull (p-u).

questions.questionText:
Look at this dictionary entry:  
child /tʃaɪld/ noun: a young person.  
What does 'noun' tell you?

options.label: A
options.text: that it is an action word

options.label: C
options.text: that it names a person or thing

questions.explanation: 'Noun' tells you the word names a person, place or thing.

questions.questionText: The guide words on a dictionary page are 'garden' and 'gold'. Which word would NOT be found on this page?
questions.explanation: The page runs from garden to gold; giraffe, glove and goat all sit between them, but guitar starts with gu-, which comes after gold, so it is on the next page.
